title: Air Ticket Fare Brands: Earlier Reworks and the Loading on a Cancellation Penalty
content:
A ticket sold under Air Ticket Fare Brands that has already been reworked carries a loading on the penalty owed for one traveller when the booking is given up. The desk counts the voluntary changes charged on the ticket in the last twelve months, and that count selects the loading.

**Basis of judgement.** What is counted is a voluntary change charged on the ticket, and only those charged within the last twelve months. A voluntary change charged earlier than twelve months back does not enter the count.

| Voluntary changes charged on the ticket in the last twelve months | Added to the penalty owed for one traveller |
| --- | --- |
| exactly one | the once-reworked loading of 25.00 US dollars is added to the penalty owed for one traveller |
| two or more | the twice-reworked loading of 45.00 US dollars is added to the penalty owed for one traveller instead |
| none | nothing is added to the penalty owed for one traveller for an earlier rework |

**The count either side of its steps.** A ticket on which no voluntary change has been charged in the last twelve months takes no addition to the penalty owed for one traveller for an earlier rework. A ticket on which one voluntary change has been charged in that period adds 25.00 US dollars to the penalty owed for one traveller. A second such change carries the loading added to that figure to 45.00 US dollars, and where three or four voluntary changes have been charged in the last twelve months the loading remains 45.00 US dollars, the two-or-more line being the last of the bands. Where exactly one voluntary change stands within the last twelve months and a further one stands from an earlier period, the count is one and the loading added to the penalty owed for one traveller is 25.00 US dollars.

The loading is a sum in dollars, and it is added to the penalty owed for one traveller.
